title: Exact Key-Recovery Security of 2EM-1 and 2EM-2
summary: A proved lower bound and known upper bound leave a gap for 2EM-1 and 2EM-2; determine their exact key-recovery security and a tight data–time tradeoff.

formal_statement.body: Determine the exact key-recovery security of the minimal two-round Even--Mansour ciphers $\mathrm{2EM\text{-}1}$ and $\mathrm{2EM\text{-}2}$ by closing the gap between the proved lower bound and the known upper bound on their data--time complexity, thereby obtaining a tight data--time tradeoff for key recovery.

scope.domain: Structural cryptanalysis of key recovery for the minimal two-round Even–Mansour ciphers 2EM-1 and 2EM-2.
parameters: Data complexity: amount of data used by a key-recovery attack
Time complexity: computational work of a key-recovery attack
scope.unresolved_remainder: Close the gap between the proved lower bound and known upper bound to establish the exact key-recovery security and a tight data–time tradeoff for both ciphers.

citations.label: New Key Recovery Attacks on Minimal Two-Round Even-Mansour Ciphers

progress.summary: The paper explicitly states that the accurate security of the two-round construction remains unknown because its proved lower bound and presented upper bound do not meet. Its new attacks narrow the upper-bound gap but do not establish a matching lower bound.
citation_labels: Takanori Isobe et al., New Key Recovery Attacks on Minimal Two-Round Even-Mansour Ciphers
